source.title: Learning biologically relevant features in a pathology foundation model using sparse autoencoders
source.citation: Nhat Dinh Minh Le et al., 2024
source.authors: Nhat Dinh Minh Le; Ci-Yue Shen; Neel Patel; Chintan Shah; Darpan Sanghavi; B. Martin; Alfred Eng; Daniel Shenker; Harshith Padigela; Raymond Biju; S. A. Javed; Jennifer A. Hipp; J. Abel; Harsha Pokkalla; S. Grullon; D. Juyal

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: The study discusses polysemanticity and reports results on pathology-model embedding dimensions and SAE features, but it does not measure individual model neurons or test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper inspects and measures residual-stream embedding dimensions and learned SAE dimensions, not individual neurons. Its results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. References to prior work are not study results.
record.test_reason: The study treats polysemanticity and superposition as motivation for training SAEs and mainly reports its SAE's performance. Its only polysemanticity observation concerns CLS-token residual-stream embedding coordinates of a pathology ViT, not neurons. That is a related but different construct, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that single embedding dimensions are polysemantic, composing higher-order pathology concepts from atomic properties, and that an SAE extracts relatively monosemantic biological features. They also report that cell-type features emerge in later layers, are absent from DINO, are robust to scanner and stain, and generalize to CPTAC.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses manual inspection of pathology-model residual-stream embeddings and sparse autoencoders, rather than the neuron-level visualization approach associated with the original circuit source.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported associations vary across PLUTO layers: color-feature associations are stronger in earlier layers, while cell-feature associations increase in later layers; the plasma-cell SAE representation is reported to emerge at layer 10. The paper also reports differences between the PLUTO and DINO pretrained models and across evaluation datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: In a pathology ViT (PLUTO), most output-layer residual-stream CLS embedding coordinates mix several visual properties (cell size, background stain, shape), judged by inspecting activation-extreme patches. Selected SAE features correlate more selectively with single cell-type counts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-stream embedding coordinates of vision transformers combine multiple image properties, and SAEs recover more selective features.

record.problems: The embedding-dimension inspection is qualitative and uses a small sample of patches at activation extremes. The study does not test model neurons or establish that the mixed characteristics are unrelated. It does not report uncertainty estimates for the correlations or entropy comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; all retained rows are within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No neurons in image classifiers are examined. Only residual-stream embedding coordinates of a self-supervised pathology ViT are inspected, and they are not shown to respond to unrelated inputs.
No language models or MLP neurons are studied.
Superposition is cited, but capacity pressure is not tested.
No test of initialization, regularization or training noise.
No comparison of polysemantic-neuron share across activation functions or architectures. The PLUTO-vs-DINO comparison concerns SAE features' cell correlations.
Shared-feature readings of canonical polysemantic neurons are not examined.
Activation ranges and explanation scoring are not varied for polysemanticity judgments.

record.verdict_notes: The CLS residual-stream basis is not a privileged neuron basis, so 'polysemantic dimensions' here differs from polysemantic neurons. The paper itself frames the combinations as coherent pathology concepts (e.g. epithelium vs stroma), which is closer in spirit to V6, but it involves no neurons. Polysemanticity is assessed from 10 randomly sampled patches per dimension, with no counts or controls.

versions.untested_parts: Tests SAE and residual-stream embedding dimensions in a pathology ViT, not individual neurons in image classifiers or responses to unrelated input categories.
No language models, MLP neurons, or token/context responses.
The paper cites the Superposition Hypothesis but does not test feature capacity pressure or a causal superposition mechanism.
No test of initialization, regularization, or training noise producing polysemantic neurons when capacity is sufficient.
The study does not compare the share of polysemantic neurons across activation functions or architectures, or test whether that share can be lowered without performance loss.
It does not investigate whether canonical polysemantic neurons detect a shared feature or whether their apparent mixtures are related offshoots of one job.
It does not compare polysemanticity judgments across activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods.

rows.subject: PLUTO ViT-S
rows.operation_detail: Manually inspected patches at the low and high activation extremes of each output-layer embedding dimension.

conditions.value: 5 patches from each of the lowest 5% and highest 5% activation values per dimension

rows.measure: Visual inspection of the image characteristics associated with embedding dimension 27
rows.value: Dimension 27 was more activated for larger cells, purple rather than red backgrounds, and non-elongated cell shapes.
rows.note: This is a reported mixture of image characteristics in an embedding coordinate, not a measurement of a neuron.
rows.check: The subject is a residual-stream (CLS) embedding coordinate, not a neuron. The mixed properties (cell size, background colour, shape) are not shown to be unrelated, so the measure cannot show the V1 effect.

rows.subject: PLUTO ViT-S
rows.operation_detail: Manually inspected patches at the low and high activation extremes of each output-layer embedding dimension.

conditions.value: 5 patches from each of the lowest 5% and highest 5% activation values per dimension

rows.measure: Visual inspection of the image characteristics associated with embedding dimension 118
rows.value: Dimension 118 was more activated for mucinous and round structures and less activated for fibrous structures.
rows.note: The paper describes multiple characteristics for this embedding coordinate; it does not assess whether they are unrelated.
rows.check: Same issue as r1. The properties are an embedding-coordinate description, not a neuron response to unrelated inputs.

rows.subject: PLUTO ViT-S
rows.operation_detail: Manually inspected activation-extreme patches for each embedding dimension.
rows.measure: Qualitative prevalence of dimensions encoding combinations of image characteristics
rows.value: The authors state that most embedding dimensions encoded combinations of cellular, tissue, and background-stain characteristics.
rows.note: No numerical fraction is reported for 'most'; the paper characterizes some combinations as complex pathology-relevant concepts.
rows.check: This is a qualitative 'most dimensions' statement about embedding coordinates, with no fraction given. The authors say the combinations form coherent pathology concepts, not unrelated mixtures.

rows.subject: PLUTO ViT-S and PLUTO SAE
rows.stage_stated: pretrained frozen encoder; SAE trained on embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Compared cell-count correlations of PLUTO embedding dimension 148 with SAE dimension 1736.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation with plasma cell counts
rows.note: This compares feature-to-cell-count associations; it is not a neuron polysemanticity measurement.
rows.check: This row compares the study's own method (an SAE feature) with a raw embedding dimension. It is a method-performance comparison, not a polysemanticity rate. The dimensions were also selected as the best plasma-cell correlates, so these are selection values.

rows.subject: PLUTO ViT-S and PLUTO SAE
rows.stage_stated: pretrained frozen encoder; SAE trained on embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Compared entropy of cell-type correlation distributions for PLUTO embedding dimension 148 and SAE dimension 1736.
rows.measure: Entropy of the distribution of absolute correlations with five cell-class densities
rows.baseline: PLUTO embedding dimension 148: S = 0.65; maximum possible Smax = 0.70
rows.note: The authors interpret lower entropy as greater monosemanticity with respect to the five measured cell concepts.
rows.check: This is an own-method comparison on one selected dimension pair, using an entropy over five cell types. It is not a measurement of neuron polysemanticity.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
